sections.html:
Locals call Springville Art City, and it is where you will find the Springville Museum of Art. The city lies under the western slope of the Wasatch Range in Utah County, roughly 3 miles from Utah Lake's average shoreline. It spans 14.4 square miles at 4,554 feet and lies nearly all east of Interstate 15.

The 2020 Census counted 35,268 people, which is 19.7% more than the 29,466 of 2010. Owners live in about 71.7% of homes. For 2020 to 2024 the median home value is $454,400 and median gross rent is $1,572. Condition and lot size will move your own number up or down from that survey median.

Many residents commute to jobs in Provo-Orem and Salt Lake City, and commercial, office and industrial growth is expected along the I-15 corridor. Provo is also where you will find the county assessor, treasurer and recorder. Nebo School District covers Springville.

Springville High School, Springville Junior High, Spring Canyon Middle School and several elementary schools belong to Nebo. Families also look at Reagan Academy and Merit Academy, both charters, and the Elizabeth DeLong School campus of the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind is in town. Food production and manufacturing are the best-known employers, among them Stouffer Foods with more than 500 employees and Valtek with more than 400.

sections.h2: Renting out part of a house: ADU rules
sections.html:
The city allows an ADU only in single-family residential zones, so duplexes, twin homes and apartments are out. Ownership and occupancy conditions apply.

ADU topicSpringville rule
OwnershipOwner must hold at least 50% of the property
OccupancyMain house or ADU must be owner-occupied; both cannot be rentals
PermitBuilding permit for interior conversions and detached ADUs
Short-term rental under 30 daysCity business license; host lives in the main dwelling and is present

Whether you can rent the top and bottom of a house to separate tenants turns on the zone, and on whether the second unit was legally permitted or counts as a legal nonconforming use. A basement apartment that never got a permit is something the buyer should hear about before signing.

You need a building permit before you enlarge, repair, alter, add to or demolish a structure, or install equipment in it. The city building division lists state guidelines for exempt work.

Expect an inspection within three business days of asking; same-day slots are not available. Anything requested after 5:00 p.m. Friday through Sunday night is treated as a Monday request. Call the building office at 801-489-2704. Remodeled without a permit? Lenders and inspectors notice, so get your permit history from the city first.

Springville operates its own power, water and public works. The Springville Power Department runs the Whitehead Power Plant, offers a Customer Generation program for solar systems, and takes outage and billing calls at (801) 489-2750. An annual water quality report is linked from the culinary water page, and recycling pickup follows an alternating two-week schedule. A buyer moving in will need city utility accounts, so put that on your closing checklist.

Inspectors in Springville may raise either subject. The nearby Wasatch Fault has ten segments with five active, the Provo segment among them, and a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake has an estimated 57% chance of striking within 50 years. As for radon, the state says one in three Utah homes tests high, with 4 picocuries per liter as the action level. A short test ahead of listing keeps the result from surprising you mid-sale.

Utah County does the billing here. November 30 is the final day without a penalty, and the Auditor sends a valuation notice every year, with the tax notice itself landing sometime from mid to late October.

Think the value is wrong? The Board of Equalization takes your filing until September 15 or 45 days after the notice date, whichever is later, and after that the value is locked in for the year. Owners living in the house get a 45% exemption.

The Treasurer sits at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1200, Provo (801-851-8255). Ask there for a payoff number, since delinquencies from earlier years are left off the bill. Deeds are filed by the Recorder in Suite 1300, 801-851-8179.

With no mortgage, nothing waits on an appraisal or a loan decision. Tell us about the house, read the written offer, and name a closing date. Title or escrow staff run the closing, and the deed goes to Provo for recording. Mention any unpermitted ADU or addition at the outset.

Whatever you owe in back taxes is taken out of your proceeds at the closing table, while the year in progress is split with the buyer by days of ownership. Old delinquencies hide from the current bill, so call the Treasurer for the real payoff number before settling on a price. The appeal deadline above still applies if a sale is pending and the value looks high.

sections.h2: A cash sale, step by step
sections.html:
Send the address along with what you know: the roof, the furnace, any ADU, any remodel done without a permit. An offer follows. When it tops a listing's net after commissions and repairs, you set the date, and the title company starts a file and hunts for liens. You sign, the deed is recorded, and the proceeds reach you once payoffs are made.

Pack photo ID, a loan payoff statement if one applies, the newest tax notice, permit papers for any addition or ADU, and the keys. A cash buyer will not ask you to repaint, replace carpet or work through a punch list.

Selling on the market may bring a higher price from a financed buyer when the house is in good order and you have time. Cash is the better fit with unpermitted work, a basement unit short on paperwork, sitting tenants, or an inherited home still full of belongings. Get the offer, weigh it against a plausible listing result, and make your call. You may decline.

Gather the paperwork a buyer will ask about before anyone walks through. That means permit history for any remodel, the ADU permit and owner-occupancy details if there is a second unit, and any short-term rental license you held. Disclose gaps in the paperwork early, because a surprise found late in a deal usually costs more than a problem you named up front. If you are not sure whether work was permitted, ask the city building office before you list.

• A basement apartment with no permit or no clear owner-occupancy history.
  • Short-term renting by a host who lived elsewhere.
  • A remodel finished without a building permit.
  • Furniture and belongings still sitting in an inherited house.

faqs.a: Yes. Utah County handles valuation, tax billing and deed recording, and Nebo School District serves the city.

faqs.q: When are Springville property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without a penalty. Utah County mails the tax notice between mid and late October.

faqs.q: Can I have a basement apartment in Springville?
faqs.a: Only as a permitted ADU in a single-family zone. The owner must own at least 50% and live in either the main house or the ADU, and a building permit is required.

faqs.q: How many people live in Springville?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 35,268 people, up 19.7% from 29,466 in 2010.

faqs.q: Do I need a license for a short-term rental in Springville?
faqs.a: Yes. Rentals under 30 days need a city business license, and the host must live in the main dwelling and be present.
